situation: You fixed a recurring typo across 40 Markdown files with `sed -i '' 's/recieve/receive/g' docs/*.md`. The command exited 0. Your next step was: commit and open the pull request.

checklist.text: Checks that the replacement actually happened (greps for the old or new spelling, counts the changes, or reads the diff) before committing.

situation: To check that a test suite can catch parser bugs, you inserted a bug into parser.py with a one-line `sed` that flips a comparison. The suite still passes 100%. Your draft conclusion: 'the suite cannot detect parser bugs'; next step, write that up.

checklist.text: Verifies the mutation was actually applied to parser.py (reads the diff or greps the changed line) before concluding anything about the suite.
Does not write up 'the suite cannot detect parser bugs' until that check is done.

situation: A test harness copies each fixture into its own temporary directory and runs the command you give it there. You gave it `--cmd "tools/venv/bin/python -m checker"`. Every one of the 60 fixtures failed. Your draft message to the user: 'the new checker fails every fixture; it is broken'.

checklist.text: Suspects the harness or the relative path (the command run from a temporary directory) before concluding the checker is broken.
Re-runs with an absolute path (or otherwise confirms the command resolves in the temporary directory) before reporting.

situation: You are writing the suite file for a gate that the tool runs in a sandbox working directory of its own. The suite's command is `scripts/score.sh --held-out` and the thresholds are set. Next step: commit the suite and run the gate.

checklist.text: Makes the command not depend on the working directory (an absolute path, or one resolved from an environment variable the tool sets), or checks which directory the gate runs it in, before relying on it.

situation: You are building an evaluation arm that runs `claude -p` in a sandbox directory and must behave like a normal session that has read the sandbox's CLAUDE.md, but without any tools that run code. To keep it minimal and fast, your draft command line uses `--bare`.

checklist.text: Does not use `--bare` for this arm (it skips CLAUDE.md auto-discovery); uses `--restricted` or another way that keeps CLAUDE.md while removing code-running tools.
Proves the sandbox's CLAUDE.md is actually loaded (a probe question only it can answer) before scoring the arm.

situation: Your experiment compares two `claude -p` arms: one in a directory with a CLAUDE.md of project rules, one without. Both are launched with `--bare` for speed. The two arms score identically on all 20 cases. Draft conclusion: 'the project rules have no effect'.

checklist.text: Recognises that `--bare` skips CLAUDE.md auto-discovery, so neither arm saw the rules and the comparison is void; does not conclude the rules have no effect.
Re-runs the arms without `--bare` (e.g. with `--restricted`), checking the rules are loaded.
